description: Public screening ranges for controls-retrofit savings by retrofit class. These are literature-derived plausibility bands, NOT guarantees or measured results for any specific building: use them to sanity-check proxy/EnergyPlus estimates, never to publish savings. Percentages are fractions of the stated savings_basis. Entries whose sources include kind=screening_placeholder are synthetic anchors awaiting a public citation and always carry confidence=low.

classes.label: Equipment scheduling / start-stop optimization
classes.applicability: Buildings with 24/7 or over-scheduled HVAC/lighting versus actual occupancy; savings scale with excess run hours.

sources.title: Mills (LBNL), Building Commissioning: A Golden Opportunity for Reducing Energy Costs and Greenhouse Gas Emissions (2009)
sources.note: Existing-building commissioning median whole-building savings 16%, median payback 1.1 yr; scheduling fixes are the most common measure family.

sources.title: PNNL-25985, Impacts of Commercial Building Controls on Energy Savings and Peak Load Reduction (2017)
sources.note: Shortened HVAC schedules among the highest-impact individual control corrections in the national packaged/RTU analysis.

classes.label: Supply-air temperature (discharge air) reset
classes.applicability: VAV systems with fixed 55 F discharge; interacts with reheat (gas down, fan/cooling shifts) so quote fuel-by-fuel.

sources.title: ASHRAE Guideline 36 High-Performance Sequences of Operation for HVAC Systems (public overview material)
sources.note: Trim-and-respond SAT reset is a core G36 sequence; savings shown in field/simulation studies vary strongly by climate and reheat design.

sources.title: Screening placeholder band pending a dedicated public SAT-reset field-study citation
sources.note: Band is a synthetic anchor consistent with G36 simulation literature; treat as low confidence.

classes.label: Duct static pressure reset (fan-law savings)
classes.applicability: VAV air handlers with VFDs holding a fixed static setpoint; savings follow the cube-law on the pressure ratio.

sources.title: PNNL-25985, Impacts of Commercial Building Controls on Energy Savings and Peak Load Reduction (2017)
sources.note: Advanced RTU/AHU controls incl. fan-speed optimization show large fan-energy fractions; band expressed on fan energy only.

classes.label: Hot-water supply temperature reset
classes.applicability: Hydronic heating plants running design HWST year-round; condensing boilers gain extra efficiency at low return temps.

sources.title: DOE Better Buildings / Building America publications on hydronic reset controls (public program guidance)
sources.note: Program guidance cites single-digit heating-fuel percentages for outdoor-air-reset on hydronic loops; exact figure is climate/plant dependent.

sources.title: Screening placeholder band pending a plant-level public measurement citation
sources.note: Synthetic anchor consistent with the WattLab hydronic_reset_bins ladder defaults (max ~5% of load in mild bins).

classes.label: Chilled-water supply temperature reset
classes.applicability: Water-cooled or air-cooled chiller plants at fixed design CHWST; ~1-2% chiller kW per degree F of reset is the classic rule of thumb, capped by dehumidification needs.

sources.title: DOE/FEMP Operations & Maintenance Best Practices Guide, Release 3.0 (chiller chapter)
sources.note: Public O&M guidance describes CHW reset as a standard low-cost chiller efficiency measure; percentage band here is a screening synthesis, not a quoted table.

sources.title: Screening placeholder band; no single public field-measured range adopted yet
sources.note: Treat as low confidence until a plant-specific bin calculation or public study replaces it.

classes.label: Condenser-water temperature reset / tower optimization
classes.applicability: Water-cooled plants with fixed CW setpoints well above achievable wet-bulb approach; net savings must account for added tower fan energy.

sources.title: Screening placeholder band pending a public condenser-water optimization study citation
sources.note: Synthetic anchor from the ~1-1.5% chiller kW per degree F condenser-relief rule of thumb; verify with a plant model before quoting.

classes.label: Air-side economizer repair / enable
classes.applicability: Units with stuck/disabled dampers or failed sensors in economizer-favorable climates; savings basis is mechanical cooling energy.

sources.title: PNNL-25985, Impacts of Commercial Building Controls on Energy Savings and Peak Load Reduction (2017)
sources.note: Economizer faults are among the most common and highest-impact packaged-unit control problems in the national analysis.

classes.label: Demand-controlled ventilation (CO2-based)
classes.applicability: High and variable occupancy spaces ventilated at design rates (assembly, classrooms); savings concentrate in heating climates.

sources.title: PNNL-25985, Impacts of Commercial Building Controls on Energy Savings and Peak Load Reduction (2017)
sources.note: DCV modeled as part of the advanced-controls package for packaged systems.

classes.label: VAV box minimum-flow reduction (G36-style)
classes.applicability: Legacy VAV boxes at 30-50% minimums that can be reset to ~10-20%; cuts reheat (gas) and fan energy simultaneously.

sources.title: ASHRAE Guideline 36 High-Performance Sequences of Operation for HVAC Systems (public overview material)
sources.note: Reduced minimums with dual-max logic are central to G36; HVAC-energy study savings around ~30% are frequently cited for full G36 packages, less for minimums alone.

classes.label: Full Guideline 36 airside package (resets + minimums + requests)
classes.applicability: Built-up VAV systems with DDC capable of trim-and-respond; whole-building percentage is much lower than the HVAC-only figure — never conflate them.

sources.title: LBNL field demonstration reporting on ASHRAE Guideline 36 sequences (public summary: average ~31% HVAC energy savings)
sources.note: HVAC-only average from public LBNL demonstration summaries; individual sites vary widely (roughly 10-45%).

classes.label: Pneumatic-to-DDC controls conversion
classes.applicability: Buildings still on pneumatic thermostats/actuators; enables scheduling and resets and eliminates most control-air compressor runtime.

sources.title: GSA / DOE public retrofit case-study literature on pneumatic-to-DDC conversions
sources.note: Case studies report double-digit whole-building savings when conversion unlocks scheduling/reset capability; range here is a screening synthesis.

sources.title: Screening placeholder band pending a specific public measured-savings citation
sources.note: Savings depend on what sequences the new DDC actually implements; treat as low confidence.
